name: key-caster
description: Lightweight on-screen keystroke displayer for Linux (Wayland, COSMIC, X11) inspired by KeyCastr
readme_summary: Key-caster is a lightweight, on-screen keystroke displayer for Linux that shows your key presses visually. It's designed to be unobtrusive and works across Wayland, COSMIC, and X11 environments, offering features like configuration persistence and privacy controls.
key_features: Lightweight on-screen keystroke displayer
Supports Wayland, COSMIC, and X11
Non-root execution via input group
Per-device hardware layout routing
Robust device hotplugging
Configuration persistence (position, layout, opacity)
Privacy masking and global capture pause
Customizable font size, opacity, position, and layout
primary_use_case: To visually display keystrokes on-screen for Linux users, particularly useful for screen recording, live streaming, or demonstrating keyboard usage.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, translucent digital ghost character, representing 'Key-caster', hovering near a keyboard. As fingers (represented by abstract, glowing wisps) touch the keys, the ghost instantly materializes the pressed key's symbol as a clean, glowing glyph in the air above the keyboard. The scene is a cozy, dimly lit study, with subtle digital particles flowing from the keyboard to the ghost. A small, minimalist UI element resembling a transparent overlay shows the sequence of recently pressed keys. The overall mood is helpful and unobtrusive. Rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with a soft, ethereal glow and a focus on clarity and simplicity.

name: murces
description: Minecraft server TUI for Linux servers meant to be used over ssh.
readme_summary: MurCes is a high-performance, zero-overhead TUI and CLI manager for dedicated Minecraft servers on Linux and WSL2. It offers a lightweight alternative to heavy web panels, providing features like native binary compilation, detached process supervision, integrated mod management, safe world backups, and zero-config port forwarding.
key_features: Native Ahead-of-Time (AOT) Binary via GraalVM Native Image for fast startup and low memory usage
Portable OpenJDK Provisioning for on-demand Java runtime downloads
Detached Process Supervision using tmux for server resilience
Modern Terminal Aesthetics with 24-bit TrueColor support and customizable themes
Built-in Mod Ecosystem integration with Modrinth and CurseForge for easy mod management and updates
Safe World State Flushing for reliable backups
Zero-Config Port Forwarding with Playit.gg integration
Player Access Control for whitelist and ban management
primary_use_case: Managing dedicated Minecraft servers on Linux/WSL2 environments, especially on resource-constrained systems like VPS or homelabs, by providing a lightweight, feature-rich terminal-based interface.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled alchemist in a dimly lit, cozy workshop, meticulously tending to a glowing, miniature Minecraft world contained within a glass orb. The alchemist uses a set of intricate, glowing tools to adjust elements within the orb, such as adding digital 'mod' components or 'flushing' the world state for a safe backup. Small, stylized terminal windows float around the orb, displaying server status and player counts. The overall scene should evoke a sense of control, efficiency, and a touch of magic in managing a complex digital entity. The art style should be a 3D isometric illustration with warm, inviting lighting and a focus on detailed, yet clean, visual elements, with the name 'MurCes' subtly etched onto a workbench.

name: AutoMagik
description: A python app to create autostart profiles on Linux.
readme_summary: AutoMagik is a Python application designed to simplify the creation and management of autostart profiles on Linux systems. It allows users to select predefined profiles, each configured to launch a specific list of programs for a particular task, streamlining the startup process for various workflows.
key_features: Create autostart profiles for Linux
Select profiles to launch specific program lists
Personal utility for task-specific program startup
Tested on Fedora 44 KDE
primary_use_case: To automate the launching of specific sets of applications on a Linux system based on user-defined profiles, thereby streamlining workflows for different tasks.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly robot assistant in a cozy study, holding a tablet displaying a 'Profile Selection' menu. The robot is gesturing towards a desk where several distinct workstations are automatically powering on and launching relevant applications: one for coding (IDE, terminal), one for design (graphics software, color palette), and one for media (music player, video editor). Subtle glowing lines connect the selected profile on the tablet to each workstation. The AutoMagik logo is visible on the robot's chassis. The scene is bright and organized, rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with a warm color palette.

name: maltrail
readme_summary: Maltrail is a network traffic detection system that identifies malicious infrastructure communication and network anomalies by matching observed network data against a set of indicators called 'trails'. It consists of a Rust-based sensor for traffic capture and detection, and a Python server for reporting, event intake, and API access.
key_features: Comprehensive trail set combining static, public feeds, and custom indicators
Multithreaded Rust sensor with libpcap and optional PACKET_FANOUT
Python server for reporting interface, event intake, and HTTP API
Plain-text custom trails and whitelists for version control
Heuristic detections for various suspicious network activities
Multiple logging options including local, remote, CEF, and Logstash JSON
Deployment validation and Prometheus metrics support
primary_use_case: Network traffic monitoring and detection of malicious infrastructure communication and anomalies.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant digital lighthouse keeper standing on a rocky outcrop, scanning the dark, stormy sea of network traffic with a powerful, glowing beam. The beam illuminates suspicious ships (malicious IPs/domains) with red warning lights, while safe vessels pass by unnoticed. Small, glowing data streams representing network packets flow towards the lighthouse. The lighthouse itself subtly incorporates the 'Maltrail' name and has small screens showing network activity logs. The scene is set at night with dramatic lighting, emphasizing the protective and watchful nature of the system. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a dark, tech-noir color palette and clear, defined elements.

name: VisoMaster-Fusion
description: Powerful & Easy-to-Use Video Face Swapping and Editing Software
readme_summary: VisoMaster Fusion is a desktop application for AI-powered face swapping, enhancement, and editing across images, videos, and live webcam feeds. It offers a user-friendly graphical interface combined with advanced model controls, batch processing, and GPU acceleration for efficient video manipulation.
key_features: AI-powered face swapping and editing
Support for images, videos, and live webcam feeds
Multiple swapper models (Inswapper128, InStyleSwapper, SimSwap, etc.)
Multi-face workflows with tracking and similarity thresholding
Face likeness, keypoint replacement, expression editing, and pose controls
Masking tools (occlusion, XSeg, face parser, etc.)
Face restoration and enhancement (GFPGAN, frame enhancers)
ReF-LDM Denoiser
Video timeline markers and job manager for batch processing
GPU-accelerated inference (CUDA, TensorRT)
Portable launcher with maintenance tools
primary_use_case: AI-powered video face swapping and editing for desktop users.
cover_image_prompt: A digital sculptor in a brightly lit, modern workshop, meticulously reshaping a clay bust of a person. The sculptor uses glowing, ethereal tools that project holographic interfaces showing different facial features and expressions. On one side, a video feed displays the original face, while on the other, the sculpted bust transforms to match the desired features. Subtle data streams and code snippets flow around the workshop, indicating the AI's involvement. The overall mood is creative and transformative, highlighting the power of AI to alter and enhance facial appearances in video. The art style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clean lines and a vibrant, futuristic color palette, emphasizing the 'VisoMaster Fusion' name subtly integrated into the workshop's machinery.
